utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. I do not know if the Defence has something to say on the subject. Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fourmy. And I -- and my thanks to my learned friend for raising the matter. Yes, we talked about it yesterday, and our -- the concern is shared, but we already did so at the Status Conference, so I do not have anything else to add to what my learned friend has said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I fully agree with my friends from the Prosecution and Mr. Krsnik, but I'd support that by saying that the Defence really insists on getting, at the earliest possible day - that is, if possible, even today - to get the list of witnesses for the main hearing so that we can prepare and step up our work. I believe that the reasonable deadline for the submission of this material is long past. Of course, we do not hold it against our learned friends, and we support their attitude, because we think that between today and the 10th of September, there isn't really much time, and that is when the main hearing should start. And I am afraid that the Defence is already suffering because it has not received this documentation. Therefore, I also second the suggestion to defer the main hearing. That would also enable the Prosecution to disclose to us the final list and order of appearance of witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Seric. Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fourmy. I mean, I know that you saw the record of the Status Conference and I heard the instructions of the Honourable Judge Wald. We resolved a number of things there, so that I do not have anything else to add to this, and I fully share the opinion of my colleagues and second it also. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor, as regards the list of witnesses? Because I believe this is the only document that you need now. As for the rest of disclosures, I believe there are no other -- at least, I hope there are no problems regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Fourmy, counsel are correct. Of course, the record will speak for itself. At the Status Conference with Judge Wald, the agreement was that the Prosecution would provide notice of the first batch, if you will, some first group of witnesses, in terms of the order that they would be called, and we have certainly agreed to do that and have every intention of doing that. We also intend, in the very near future, to file an amended or further 65 ter witness list, and that's being worked on as I -- literally as I speak. So those things are in progress. But again -- and I do not withdraw from those commitments for one moment. But again, that brings us back to the question of the trial date, and certain disclosures that are in connection with it work backwards from a trial date, and that again just highlights the importance of having a firm date as soon as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Prosecutor. I do not wish to detain you too long here, but only a few words, and very quickly. You know that indeed the 10th of September was repeatedly mentioned. To my knowledge, this date is still valid. The main hearing should take place before a Chamber consisting of one permanent Judge and two ad litem Judges. It is therefore necessary for these two Judges to be nominated, and they are about to be. That is, a group of ad litem Judges will be able to undertake their duties, I believe, on the 1st of September. I'm not sure of the date, but that will happen shortly. They're about to be designated, and it is only now that the President of the Tribunal will be able to organise the Chambers which will then hear the cases. What I am telling you now is the only information that I have available. With Madam Registrar, I will communicate your concerns as to the exact date of the beginning of the trial, both to the Registrar, to the Deputy Registrar, and the President and his office. And rest assured that we shall do whatever is within our power so that the definitive date, in inverted brackets, but that the date be communicated to you. Insofar as the organisation of your work is concerned, the planning of witnesses and all that, I believe it is absolutely fundamental that you perceive of the 10th of September as the date of the beginning of the trial. Having said that, the Prosecutor, evidently, the sooner you can communicate the list of witnesses, at least the group, and the sooner you finalise the list of witnesses, with that date in mind, the better it will be for the Defence and their preparation. I apologise that I cannot be more precise. If anyone -- if I receive any other information, rest assured that I will communicate it to you. Witness M, we apologise to you. There are always matters to deal with in this Tribunal. It is not always done at the most opportune moments. But thank you very much. I wish to thank the technical booth, and especially the court reporters, the court reporters and reporteresses, for resolving technical problems. I also wish to thank the interpreters. We shall be back here tomorrow morning at 9.15. Thank you very much, Witness, and please stay in your seat until the usher helps you to leave the courtroom. Thank you. Until tomorrow. The session is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: 12.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of August, 2001, at 9.15 a.m.
